sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.28251 Of 2015
Order:

This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondent No.4 in trying to dispossess the petitioner from the land admeasuring approximately Ac.1.00 Guntas in Sy.No.47/24/1, situated at Settharampuram Village, Pinapaka Mandal, Khammam District as illegal, arbitrary and unreasonable and consequently direct the respondents not to interfere with the land of the petitioner and pass..."

2. Heard Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri M.Sahas Reddy, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing for the respondents and perused the entire material on record.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the owner of the land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.1-00 guntas in Sy.No.47/27/1, situated at Settharampuram Village,
Pinapaka Mandal, Khammam District.
The grievance of the petitioner is that the SK,J respondent No.6 has acquired some part of the patta land of the petitioner for the purpose of construction of Bhadradri Power Plant.
After acquiring the said land, the petitioner is in possession of the remaining land to an extent of Ac.1-00 guntas and the name of the petitioner is also recorded as enjoyer in the revenue records.

Without following any procedure and without initiating the land acquisition proceedings, the respondents are trying to interfere with the possession of the petitioner and requested to allow the writ petition.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue basing on the counter submits that as per the revenue records i.e., Sethwar and Chesala Pahani, the Sy.No.47 was recorded as Government land (Sarkari), but, the petitioner stated that the said survey number is a patta land.

The petitioner is trying to grab the Government property by creating fraudulent documents and on basis of some fraudulent entries in occupant column in pahani for the year SK,J 2013-14 and the suit schedule land is a Government land.
In fact, the petitioner is not in possession of the above land at any point of time and the said land is vacant and it is in the custody of the Government and requested to dismiss the writ petition.

5. After hearing both sides and perusing the record, this Court is of the considered view that the main contention of the respondents is that the land in Sy.No.47 belongs to the Government and the petitioner at no point of time, became the owner of the property and merely basing on the wrong entries in the revenue records, the petitioner is trying to grab the land of the Government.

But, Page No.41 of the material paper of the counter filed by the respondents shows that as per Chesal Pahani,
Kandi Swetha, vs The State Of Telangana, on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43978128/
1 the land in Sy.No.47 admeasuring to an extent of Ac.157.36 guntas is a Poramboku land and the land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.43.13 guntas is a Patta land.

entities.text:
Chesal Pahani,
Kandi Swetha, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Adangal/Pahani for the year 1994-95 in Page No.51 of the material paper in the counter shows that in Sy.No.47/24, SK,J the name of the pattedar shows as Smt. Mekala Buchamma and as per Adangal/Pahani for the year 2013-14, Sy.No.47/24/1 is a patta land and Smt. Mekala Buchamma as pattadar and the name of the petitioner is shown in the enjoyer column.
Also as per Adangal/Pahani for the year 2014-15, it clearly shows that the subject land is a patta land and the name of the petitioner is shown as the enjoyer.
It clearly shows that as per the revenue records, the suit schedule property does not belong to the Government and the name of the petitioner is shown in the enjoyer column.

The respondents,
in contrary to the revenue records, stating that the suit schedule property belongs to the Government and the petitioner in no point of time became the possessor of the subject property.
6. The contention of the respondents is contrary to the revenue records and the same cannot be accepted.

As per the revenue records, the suit schedule property is a private patta land and the respondents cannot interfere with the SK,J possession of the petitioner in the suit schedule property without following due process of law, if the respondents want to acquire the land, they have to follow the procedure as contemplated under Land Acquisition Act.

7. In view of the above findings, the writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents not to interfere with the possession of the petitioner in the subject property, without following due process of law.

If the respondents want to acquire the land of the petitioner, they have to follow the procedure under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and issue notice to the petitioner.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There shall be no order as to costs.
8. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

____ JUSTICE K.SARATH Date: 12.12.2024 BB Kandi Swetha, vs The State Of Telangana, on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43978128/
